title: Making adjectives agree
description: Give an adjective the right ending for en-words, ett-words, plurals and the definite form.

guide.summary: A Swedish adjective changes its ending to match the noun: nothing for an en-word, -t for an ett-word, -a for plurals and for the definite form. Learn these three endings and the handful of special words, and you can describe anything.

sections.title: En-words and ett-words
sections.text: With an en-word the adjective is in its dictionary form. With an ett-word it adds -t. This is the same whether the adjective comes before the noun or later in the sentence.
steps: Find the noun the adjective describes.
Is it en or ett? Check the article or the dictionary.
En: use the bare adjective. Ett: add -t.
watch: The ending follows the noun, not the meaning: ett barn is a person but still takes -t.

sections.title: Plurals take -a
sections.text: In the plural the adjective adds -a for every noun, en or ett. Gender no longer matters.
steps: Is the noun plural? Look for två, många or a plural ending.
If it is, add -a to the adjective and stop.
watch: Some nouns look the same in the plural (ett hus, två hus). Let the number words decide.

sections.title: After är
sections.text: An adjective after är, blir or verkar still agrees with the subject. The subject decides: en-word bare, ett-word -t, plural -a. The definite ending of the subject does not make the adjective definite.
steps: Find the subject before är.
Ask: en-word, ett-word or plural?
Give the adjective the ending for that answer.
watch: Huset is definite, but after är the adjective is stort, not stora.
Barnen means the children, so it is plural.

sections.title: The definite form and possessives
sections.text: Before a definite noun the adjective always takes -a, and the phrase starts with den (en-words), det (ett-words) or de (plural). After a possessive such as min, din or vår the adjective also takes -a, but the noun stays bare.
steps: Does the phrase mean the, or start with a possessive?
If so, the adjective takes -a, whatever the gender.
With the: add den, det or de in front and the ending on the noun. With a possessive: no ending on the noun.
watch: Never -t before a definite noun: det stora huset.
After a possessive the noun has no -en or -et: min nya bil.

sections.title: Spelling changes
sections.text: A few adjectives change their spelling when they take an ending. Adjectives that end in a long vowel, or in a long vowel plus -d or -t, write a double t. Adjectives in -el, -er or -en drop a letter before -a.
steps: Does it end in a long vowel, or a long vowel plus -d or -t (ny, röd, vit)? Write -tt for the ett form.
Does it end in -ig? Just add -t.
Does it end in -al, -el or -er? Drop the vowel before -a.
watch: Gammal in the plural is gamla, with one m.

sections.title: Liten, litet, lilla, små
sections.text: Small is irregular. It has four forms, and the plural is a different word.

rows: den lilla katten, min lilla bror
the small cat, my little brother

steps: Plural, with or without the? Use små.
Singular after den, det or a possessive? Use lilla.
Otherwise: liten with en, litet with ett.
watch: Små is also the definite plural: de små husen.

sections.title: Adjectives that never change
sections.text: Some adjectives keep one form everywhere. The common ones are bra, extra and gratis, and most adjectives ending in -a.
steps: Check if the adjective is bra, extra, gratis or ends in -a.
If so, write it the same with en, ett, plural and definite nouns.
watch: Never add -t to bra: ett bra hotell, not ett bratt hotell.

steps: Find the noun.
Decide en or ett.
Ett-word: add -t; en-word: bare form.
Check that the noun is plural.
Add -a to the adjective, whatever the gender.
Find the subject before är.
En-word: bare. Ett-word: -t. Plural: -a.
Ignore the definite ending on the subject.
Look for the or a possessive.
Give the adjective -a.
Add den, det or de for the; keep the noun bare after a possessive.
Work out the ending first.
Long vowel, or long vowel plus -d or -t: write -tt.
-al, -el, -er: drop the vowel before -a.
Plural: små.
Definite or after a possessive: lilla.
Else liten with en, litet with ett.
Is it bra, extra, gratis or ending in -a or -s?
Then write it unchanged.

exercises.instruction: Choose the right form of stor.

mistakes.why: The bare form goes with en-words, as in en stor bil. Hus takes ett, so the adjective needs its ett ending.
The -a form is for plurals and for the definite form. Here there is one house and the article is ett.

exercises.hint: Is hus an en-word or an ett-word?
exercises.feedback: Look at the little word before the gap: ett.
exercises.explanation: Hus is an ett-word (ett hus), so the adjective adds -t: ett stort hus.

exercises.instruction: Write the adjective in the right form.

mistakes.why: That is the en-word form. Ett rum needs the adjective to add its ett ending too.
The -a ending is for plurals and definite nouns; ett rum is one room, indefinite.

exercises.feedback: After ett, a regular adjective adds -t.
exercises.explanation: Rum is an ett-word (ett rum), so fin becomes fint: ett fint rum.

exercises.instruction: Translate into Swedish.

mistakes.why: The adjective was left in its en form. With ett the adjective takes -t as well.
Kök is an ett-word, so both the article and the adjective change.
The adjective is right but the article is not: kök takes ett.

exercises.feedback: Both the article and the adjective must show that kök is an ett-word.
exercises.explanation: Kök is an ett-word, so a big kitchen is ett stort kök.

exercises.instruction: Replace jacka with täcke and change the adjective to match. Write the whole sentence.

mistakes.why: The article changed but the adjective still has its en form. After ett it needs -t.
Täcke is an ett-word; only the noun was swapped.
That is the original sentence: jacka was never replaced.

exercises.feedback: Change the article and the adjective together.
exercises.explanation: Täcke takes ett, so en varm becomes ett varmt: ett varmt täcke.

exercises.instruction: Fix the error.

mistakes.why: That is the sentence unchanged. With ett the adjective must add -t.
Hotell really is an ett-word, so changing the article makes a new error instead of fixing the old one.

exercises.feedback: The article is right; the adjective is not.
exercises.explanation: Hotell is an ett-word, so dyr adds -t: ett dyrt hotell.

exercises.instruction: Build the sentence: We live in a big house. Leave one tile unused.
exercises.source: We live in a big house.
answers: Vi bor i ett stort hus.
Vi bor i ett stor hus.
mistakes.why: That tile is the en form. The tile to leave out is the one without the ett ending.

exercises.feedback: Only one form of big fits after ett.
exercises.explanation: Hus takes ett, so big is stort: ett stort hus.

exercises.instruction: Choose the right form of varm.

mistakes.why: That is the singular en form, as in en varm tröja. There are two jumpers here.
The -t form is for one ett-word. Tröjor is plural, and plurals ignore en and ett.

exercises.feedback: Tröjor is plural.
exercises.explanation: In the plural every adjective takes -a, whatever the gender: två varma tröjor.

exercises.instruction: Write the adjective in the right form.

mistakes.why: The bare form is for one en-word. Grannar is plural.
The -t form is for one ett-word, not for a plural.

exercises.feedback: Plural nouns take the plural adjective.
exercises.explanation: Grannar is the plural of granne, so fin takes -a: fina grannar.

exercises.instruction: Translate into Swedish.

mistakes.why: The adjective stayed singular in front of a plural noun.
The -t ending marks one ett-word, and skor is plural.

exercises.feedback: The adjective in front of a plural noun ends in -a.
exercises.explanation: Skor is plural, so billig takes -a: billiga skor.

exercises.instruction: Make it two cats: två katter. Change the adjective too. Write the whole sentence.

mistakes.why: The noun went plural but the adjective did not.
The adjective is right, but katt must become plural as well.

exercises.feedback: Change the article, the noun and the adjective.
exercises.explanation: In the plural svart takes -a: två svarta katter.

exercises.instruction: Fix the error.

mistakes.why: That is the sentence unchanged. A plural noun needs the plural adjective.
The -t ending is only for one ett-word.

exercises.feedback: Look at the adjective in front of the plural noun.
exercises.explanation: Bilar is plural, so dyr takes -a: två dyra bilar.

exercises.instruction: Build the sentence: I have warm socks. Leave one tile unused.

mistakes.why: That tile is the ett form for one thing. The noun here is plural.

exercises.feedback: Only the plural form of warm fits.
exercises.explanation: Strumpor is plural, so varm takes -a: varma strumpor.

exercises.instruction: Choose the right form of stor.

mistakes.why: That is the en form, as in bilen är stor. Hus is an ett-word.
After är the -a form is only for plurals. One house is not plural, even though huset is definite.

exercises.hint: What kind of noun is huset: en or ett?
exercises.feedback: After är the adjective still agrees with the noun.
exercises.explanation: Huset is the definite form of ett hus, so after är the adjective takes -t: huset är stort.

exercises.instruction: Write the adjective in the right form.

mistakes.why: That is the form for one en-word. There are several tickets.
The -t form is for one ett-word, and biljetter are en-words in the plural.

exercises.feedback: The adjective after är agrees with a plural subject.
exercises.explanation: Biljetterna is plural, so after är dyr takes -a: biljetterna är dyra.

exercises.instruction: Translate into Swedish.

mistakes.why: Agreement does not stop after är: an ett-word still needs -t.
Ren has one n and simply adds -t.

exercises.feedback: The adjective after är agrees with rummet.
exercises.explanation: Rum is an ett-word, so after är ren takes -t: rummet är rent.

exercises.instruction: Replace Stolen with Bordet and change the adjective to match. Write the whole sentence.

mistakes.why: The adjective still matches stolen, an en-word.
The -a form after är is for plurals; there is one table.

exercises.feedback: The adjective after är follows the new noun.
exercises.explanation: Bord takes ett, so tung becomes tungt: bordet är tungt.

exercises.instruction: Fix the error.

mistakes.why: That is the sentence unchanged. A plural subject needs the plural adjective after är.
That changes the meaning to one child. The sentence talks about several children, so keep barnen and fix the adjective.

exercises.feedback: Barn looks the same in the plural, but barnen is plural.
exercises.explanation: Barnen is plural (the children), so trött takes -a: barnen är trötta.

exercises.instruction: Build the sentence: The apples are good. Leave one tile unused.

mistakes.why: That tile is the ett form for one thing. The apples are several.

exercises.feedback: After är the adjective matches a plural subject.
exercises.explanation: Äpplena is plural, so god takes -a: äpplena är goda.

exercises.instruction: Choose the right form of vit.

mistakes.why: That is the form for ett hus without the. With det and huset the adjective takes the definite ending.
The bare form belongs to an indefinite en-word, and huset is a definite ett-word.

exercises.feedback: After den, det or de the adjective always ends in -a.
exercises.explanation: In the definite form the adjective takes -a, even with an ett-word: det vita huset.

exercises.instruction: Write the adjective in the right form.

mistakes.why: That is the indefinite form, as in en svart väska. With den and väskan the adjective changes.
Neither is a Swedish form. After den the ending is the same for every noun.

exercises.feedback: Den + adjective + noun with -n: the adjective ends in -a.
exercises.explanation: Väskan is definite, so svart takes -a: den svarta väskan.

exercises.instruction: Translate into Swedish.

mistakes.why: Before a definite noun the adjective always takes -a, even with ett-words.
After är the adjective agrees with hus, an ett-word, so it needs -t.

exercises.hint: The big house: det + adjective + huset.
exercises.feedback: Inside the phrase the adjective is definite; after är it agrees with hus.
exercises.explanation: Det stora huset uses the -a form; after är, dyr agrees with an ett-word: dyrt.

alternatives.message: Common in speech. In writing Swedish keeps det in front: Det stora huset är dyrt.

exercises.instruction: Replace en with min and change the adjective. Write the whole sentence.
exercises.source: Det här är en ny cykel.
answers: Det här är min nya cykel.
Det här är min ny cykel.
mistakes.why: The adjective kept its indefinite form. After a possessive it takes the definite ending.

answers: Det här är mitt nya cykel.
mistakes.why: Cykel is an en-word, so the possessive is min, not mitt.

answers: Det här är min nya cykeln.
mistakes.why: After a possessive the noun stays in its bare form, without -n.

exercises.hint: After a possessive the adjective takes -a.
exercises.feedback: Min works like the: the adjective goes definite.
exercises.explanation: After min, din, vår and the other possessives the adjective takes -a: min nya cykel.

exercises.instruction: Fix the error.
exercises.source: De stor husen ligger vid havet.
answers: De stora husen ligger vid havet.
De stor husen ligger vid havet.
mistakes.why: That is the sentence unchanged. After de the adjective needs the definite ending.

answers: De stort husen ligger vid havet.
mistakes.why: The -t form is never used before a definite noun.

exercises.feedback: Check the adjective between de and husen.
exercises.explanation: In the definite form the adjective always takes -a: de stora husen.

exercises.instruction: Build the sentence: Your new jacket is nice. Leave one tile unused.

mistakes.why: That tile is the indefinite form. After a possessive the adjective takes -a.

exercises.hint: After din the adjective goes definite.
exercises.feedback: Inside the phrase the adjective follows the possessive; after är it is indefinite again.
exercises.explanation: After the possessive din, ny takes -a: din nya jacka. After är, fin agrees with an en-word and stays bare.

exercises.instruction: Choose the right form of fin.

mistakes.why: The -t form is for ett rum without a possessive. After mitt the adjective goes definite.
The bare form fits an indefinite en-word, and rum is neither.

exercises.feedback: A possessive makes the adjective definite.
exercises.explanation: After mitt the adjective takes -a, even though rum is an ett-word: mitt fina rum.

exercises.instruction: Choose the right form of ny.

mistakes.why: After a stressed vowel Swedish writes a double t here, so a single t is a misspelling.
That is the en form. Kylskåp takes ett.

exercises.feedback: Ny ends in a vowel.
exercises.explanation: An adjective that ends in a long vowel doubles the t: ny becomes nytt.

exercises.instruction: Write the adjective in the right form.

mistakes.why: The d is not kept before t. It merges into a double t.
The t is written double after the vowel ö here.
That is the en form, and paraply takes ett.

exercises.feedback: Röd does not just add -t.
exercises.explanation: Röd ends in -d after a long vowel: the d becomes t and the t is doubled, so ett rött paraply.

exercises.instruction: Translate into Swedish.

mistakes.why: Gammal drops its second a and one m before the ending.
Vacker drops the e before the ending -a.
After är the adjective agrees with a plural subject, not with one ett-word.

exercises.feedback: Gammal and vacker both shrink before the ending -a.
exercises.explanation: Gammal becomes gamla: one m and no second a. Vacker becomes vackra the same way.

exercises.instruction: Fix the error.

mistakes.why: That is the sentence unchanged. Adjectives in -ig still take -t after ett.
Only one t is added after -ig.

exercises.feedback: An adjective in -ig simply adds -t.
exercises.explanation: Golv is an ett-word, so smutsig adds -t: ett smutsigt golv.

exercises.instruction: Write the adjective in the right form.

mistakes.why: Gammal drops a letter before -a. The plural is shorter than this.
That is the singular en form, and föräldrar are two people.

exercises.feedback: The plural ending changes the spelling of the stem.
exercises.explanation: In the plural gammal takes -a and shrinks: gamla.

exercises.instruction: Choose the right form of vit.

mistakes.why: That is the en form. With ett the t must be doubled.
The -a ending is for plurals and definite nouns.

exercises.feedback: Vit ends in t already.
exercises.explanation: Vit already ends in t, and the ett form doubles it: ett vitt halsband.

exercises.instruction: Choose the right form of liten.

mistakes.why: That is the en form, and barn is an ett-word.
Små is the plural. There is one child here.

exercises.feedback: Liten has its own ett form.
exercises.explanation: Liten is irregular: with ett it is litet: ett litet barn.

exercises.instruction: Write the adjective in the right form.

mistakes.why: Liten does not take a regular -a ending. Its definite singular is its own word.
Små is the plural; there is one cat.
That is the indefinite form. With den and katten it changes.

exercises.feedback: The definite singular of liten is a different word.
exercises.explanation: In the definite singular liten becomes lilla: den lilla katten.

exercises.instruction: Translate into Swedish.

mistakes.why: That is the singular. Barnen is plural.
Lilla is the definite singular, used before a noun; after är with a plural use the plural.
Liten has no regular plural form.

exercises.hint: Small in the plural is a new word.
exercises.feedback: After är the adjective agrees with a plural subject.
exercises.explanation: The plural of liten is små: barnen är små.

exercises.instruction: Fix the error.

mistakes.why: That is the sentence unchanged. Liten is singular only.
Liten does not form a regular plural.

exercises.feedback: Liten has a different word for the plural.
exercises.explanation: The plural of liten is små: två små hundar.

exercises.instruction: Make it two tables: två bord. Change the adjective too. Write the whole sentence.

mistakes.why: The adjective is still singular.
Borden means the tables. After två the noun is indefinite.

exercises.hint: Bord stays bord in the plural.
exercises.feedback: Only the article and the adjective change.
exercises.explanation: The plural of liten is små, and bord has the same plural: två små bord.

exercises.instruction: Choose the right form of liten.

mistakes.why: That is the indefinite form. After min the adjective goes definite.
That is for an ett-word, and bror is an en-word.
Små is the plural, and there is one brother.

exercises.hint: A possessive comes before the gap.
exercises.feedback: After min the adjective takes its definite form.
exercises.explanation: After a possessive liten becomes lilla: min lilla bror.

exercises.instruction: Choose the right form of gratis.

mistakes.why: Adjectives ending in -s like this one take no ending, not even in the plural.
This adjective takes no -t either; it has one form only.

exercises.feedback: Gratis is the same in every form.
exercises.explanation: Gratis never takes an ending: biljetterna är gratis.

exercises.instruction: Write the adjective in the right form.

mistakes.why: This adjective takes no -t, even after ett: there is no brat or bratt.
This adjective takes no ending at all.

exercises.feedback: Bra stays the same everywhere.
exercises.explanation: Bra never changes: en bra bil, ett bra hotell, bra hotell.

exercises.instruction: Translate into Swedish.

mistakes.why: This adjective takes no plural ending.

exercises.feedback: Bra does not take the plural -a.
exercises.explanation: Bra is the same in every form: bra grannar.

alternatives.message: Right too: goda grannar is a common phrase. Bra grannar is the everyday way, and bra never changes.

exercises.instruction: Fix the error.

mistakes.why: That is the sentence unchanged. This adjective never takes an ending.

exercises.feedback: Gratis takes no -t.
exercises.explanation: Gratis is the same with en-words, ett-words and plurals: museet är gratis.

exercises.instruction: Build the sentence: I need an extra duvet. Leave one tile unused.

mistakes.why: That tile adds -t, but extra takes no ending.

exercises.feedback: Extra stays the same after ett.
exercises.explanation: Extra ends in -a and never changes: ett extra täcke.
